commands.name: account
commands.short: List and select linked mail accounts
commands.notes: Linked accounts share the current login. Use list to discover IDs and use <id|all> to persist the default mail filter; --account overrides it for one invocation.

subcommands.name: senders
subcommands.notes: Lists sender IDs, account IDs, email addresses, and account-default flags. --account limits the list; use an email or sender ID with compose --from or draft edit --from. Does not change the default.

subcommands.name: use
subcommands.short: Set the default linked mail account

commands.name: attachment
commands.short: List and save files from a thread
commands.notes: Subcommands: list, save. Lists downloadable attachments from every message in a known thread. Pass a returned ID to `hey attachment save <id>`.

flags.name: allow-partial
flags.desc: List what could be read of a thread that could only be read in part, with a notice saying what is missing

subcommands.name: save
subcommands.notes: Saves the attachment identified by an ID from `hey attachment list <thread-id>`. Existing files are preserved unless --force is set.

commands.name: auth
commands.short: Sign in, sign out, and check login status
commands.notes: Use status to check auth before other commands. Returns token expiry info in JSON. Use login --token for non-interactive auth.

flags.name: no-browser
flags.desc: Don't open browser, print URL instead

flags.name: stored
flags.desc: Only print stored OAuth token (ignore HEY_TOKEN env var)

commands.name: box
commands.short: List HEY boxes and their email threads
commands.notes: Accepts a box name or numeric ID. Returns email threads. Use topic_id with hey thread read, reply, and forward; use id with seen, unseen, and move. A row with kind "bundle" groups one sender's unseen threads and has no topic_id: list them with hey bundle view <id>, and every thread with that sender via hey contact threads <contact-id>. --page continues from the next_page cursor of an earlier listing of the same box.

flags.name: limit
flags.desc: Maximum number of threads to show

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.notes: Returns all mailbox types. Use --ids-only to pipe IDs to hey box view.

flags.name: limit
flags.desc: Maximum number of boxes to show

subcommands.name: view
subcommands.short: List email threads in a box
subcommands.notes: Accepts a box name or numeric ID. Returns email threads. Use topic_id with hey thread read, reply, and forward; use id with seen, unseen, and move. A row with kind "bundle" groups one sender's unseen threads and has no topic_id: list them with hey bundle view <id>, and every thread with that sender via hey contact threads <contact-id>. --page continues from the next_page cursor of an earlier listing of the same box.

flags.name: limit
flags.desc: Maximum number of threads to show

commands.name: bubble
commands.short: Bubble email threads up in the Imbox

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.short: List bubbled-up and scheduled email threads
subcommands.notes: Lists two buckets: bubbled_up, the threads back in the Imbox, and scheduled, the threads waiting in Bubble Up with bubble_up_schedule.bubble_up_at saying when. Use id with hey bubble pop; use topic_id with hey thread read. --limit caps each bucket.

flags.name: limit
flags.desc: Maximum number of threads to show per bucket

subcommands.name: pop
subcommands.notes: Accepts one or more box item IDs from hey box view output. Cancels each thread's bubble-up.

subcommands.name: up
subcommands.notes: Accepts one or more box item IDs from hey box view output. Exactly one of --now, --on, --tomorrow, --weekend and --next-week is required. --on takes a YYYY-MM-DD date; HEY bubbles the threads up at its morning hour of that day, or at its evening hour (18:00) when the date is today. --tomorrow, --weekend and --next-week land at the morning hour of tomorrow, the coming Saturday, and next Monday.

flags.name: next-week
flags.desc: Bubble the threads up Monday morning

flags.name: now
flags.desc: Bubble the threads up right away

flags.name: on
flags.desc: Bubble the threads up on a date (YYYY-MM-DD)

flags.name: tomorrow
flags.desc: Bubble the threads up tomorrow morning

flags.name: weekend
flags.desc: Bubble the threads up Saturday morning

commands.name: bulk-reply
commands.notes: Always run `hey bulk-reply preview <box-item-id>...` before sending. Send resolves the box items again, keeps HEY's name-tag content, and returns the delivery ID and undo state.

subcommands.name: preview
subcommands.short: Preview threads and recipients without sending
subcommands.notes: Read-only. Box item IDs come from `hey box view` or `hey search`. The result contains the latest replyable entry and exact To, CC, and BCC recipients for each thread.

subcommands.name: send
subcommands.short: Send one reply to multiple threads
subcommands.notes: Mutating. Preview first. Accepts a message via -m, stdin, or $EDITOR and repeatable --attach files. HEY's server-provided name-tag content is preserved.

flags.name: message-html
flags.desc: Reply message as raw HTML instead of Markdown

examples: hey bulk-reply send 12345 67890 -m "Thanks for the update."
hey bulk-reply send 12345 67890 -m "The report is attached." --attach ./report.pdf

subcommands.name: undo
subcommands.notes: Mutating. Works only while HEY's undo window remains open. The bulk reply ID is returned by `hey bulk-reply send`.

A bundle read through has no unseen threads; every thread with its sender, seen and unseen, is listed by hey contact threads <contact-id>.

A bundle read through has no unseen threads; every thread with its sender, seen and unseen, is listed by hey contact threads <contact-id>.

flags.name: limit
flags.desc: Maximum number of threads to show

commands.name: clip
commands.short: List and manage passages saved from email

HEY assigns a created clip to the source entry's account and resolves deletion by identity-owned clip ID across linked accounts; --account selects list presentation. The CLI verifies that the passage is source-backed by the entry's message content before saving it, with a 64 KiB passage limit and a 1 MiB source-validation limit. Find clip IDs with hey clip list.

commands.name: compose
commands.short: Write and send a new email
commands.notes: --from selects a configured sender email or ID from account senders; --account must agree. --from is only for new messages. Starts a new thread with --to (optionally --cc/--bcc), which requires --subject, or replies to an existing one with --thread-id, which does not. Repeatable --attach files are uploaded before sending and can be sent without body text. The body is Markdown; use --message-html to send raw HTML instead. --draft saves instead of sending — recipients become optional — and answers the draft ID for hey draft show/edit/send/delete. A new message ends with the sender's HEY name tag, as one composed in HEY does; --no-name-tag leaves it out.

flags.desc: Save as a draft instead of sending

flags.name: from
flags.desc: Configured sender email or ID (see hey account senders)

flags.desc: Message body as raw HTML instead of Markdown

flags.name: no-name-tag
flags.desc: Leave the sender's HEY name tag off a new message

flags.name: subject
flags.desc: Message subject (required for a new message)

flags.name: thread-id
flags.desc: Reply to this thread instead of starting a new one

hey compose --to alice@example.com --cc bob@example.com --bcc carol@example.org --subject "Kitchen remodel timeline" -m "Cabinets land the week of the 14th."
hey compose --to alice@example.com --subject "Q3 revenue report" -m "The numbers are attached." --attach ./report.pdf

With no field flags the body opens in $EDITOR as Markdown. A scheduled delivery is preserved.

commands.name: event
commands.notes: Subcommands: list, day, week, add, edit, delete. "What's on the schedule today?" is answered by day, not list: day and week read the span as HEY draws it, with a repeating event expanded into the occurrences inside it, over the calendars switched on in HEY. list reads what calendars hold — every calendar unless --calendar names one — and a repeating event is one row, its series, on the day the series began. An edit is not a patch on HEY's side: it resends the notes, location, link, attached email, reminders and time zones the event already carries, so notes lose their formatting and a countdown is removed unless --countdown names one again. edit <series id> changes a whole series; one day of it is edit <series id> --occurrence <occurrence_id from day/week> --apply-to current|future, which keeps the countdown and refuses to flatten notes unless --allow-plain-notes or --notes is given. --apply-to future starts a new series and requires --repeat with its complete schedule; a preset alone means forever and custom copies an existing opaque schedule (a count-based rule can restart its full count). A virtual day of an opaque custom schedule is read from HEY's Day view and refused if that view no longer serves it. A realized custom day cannot be split safely; use a virtual occurrence, edit that day alone, or edit the whole series. A realized preset occurrence moved away from its series time must be moved back with --apply-to current before a future split. Read the day again afterward for the new series id.

commands.name: reply
commands.notes: Replies to the latest entry in a thread, addressed the way HEY addresses a reply: everyone that entry was addressed to, plus its sender on the To line, minus the acting user's own addresses. Repeatable --to/--cc/--bcc flags merge explicit recipients into that prefill; --replace-recipients uses only the explicit lists. --dry-run is read-only, needs no message, and returns the resolved sender, recipients, subject, account, thread and entry. Accepts message via -m, stdin, or $EDITOR, plus repeatable --attach files; an attachment can be sent without body text. The message is Markdown; use --message-html to send raw HTML instead. --draft saves the reply as a draft, carries the resolved recipients, and answers the draft ID for hey draft show/edit/send/delete.

commands.name: screener
commands.short: Decide who gets to email you
commands.notes: Clearance IDs come from `hey screener list`, and are not contact IDs. Approving delivers everything the sender has waiting; denying hides it. Both are reversible with the opposite command. `hey screener history` shows what was already decided.

subcommands.name: approve
subcommands.notes: Clearance IDs come from `hey screener list`, not contact IDs. --box and --seen apply to one sender at a time; several IDs go through the bulk endpoint, which takes neither. Reverse with `hey screener deny <id>`.

flags.name: box
flags.desc: Deliver their email to this box instead of the Imbox

flags.name: seen
flags.desc: Mark what they already sent as seen

subcommands.name: clear
subcommands.notes: Clears the whole queue for the account, not one sender, and takes no confirmation. It decides nothing: senders reappear in The Screener on their next email, so what they already sent stays hidden until then. HEY queues the work, so `hey screener list` may still show the queue for a moment afterwards.

subcommands.name: deny
subcommands.notes: Clearance IDs come from `hey screener list`, not contact IDs. --spam also marks what they already sent as spam and trains HEY's filter on it, which is harder to undo than denying. Reverse with `hey screener approve <id>`.

flags.name: spam
flags.desc: Also mark what they sent as spam and train the filter

subcommands.name: history
subcommands.notes: Only senders already decided on — the pending queue is `hey screener list`. Change a decision with `hey screener approve <id>` or `hey screener deny <id>` using the ID from here. --page continues from the next_page cursor of an earlier listing.

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.short: List the senders waiting to be screened
subcommands.notes: Returns clearance IDs with the sender and the subject of what they sent. Feed the ID to `hey screener approve` or `hey screener deny`, and topic_id to `hey thread read` to read the thread first. Use --count for the number alone, which is a much cheaper request. --page continues from the next_page cursor of an earlier listing.

subcommands.name: delete
subcommands.short: Break up a Set Aside group
subcommands.notes: Deleting a group moves its threads to Previously Seen in the Imbox, not back into Set Aside. Use hey set-aside group remove to ungroup threads that should stay set aside.

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.short: List the groups in Set Aside
subcommands.notes: Returns group IDs with their thread counts. Use an ID with hey set-aside group view, add and delete.

subcommands.name: remove
subcommands.short: Take email threads out of their Set Aside group
subcommands.notes: Accepts box item IDs from hey set-aside view. The threads stay in Set Aside, outside any group.

subcommands.name: view
subcommands.short: List email threads in a Set Aside group
subcommands.notes: The ID comes from hey set-aside group list. Returns the group's threads; use id with hey set-aside group remove and hey move, topic_id with hey thread read. --page continues from the next_page cursor of an earlier listing of the same group.

flags.name: limit
flags.desc: Maximum number of threads to show

subcommands.name: view
subcommands.short: List email threads in Set Aside
subcommands.notes: Returns the same threads as hey box view set-aside, with each thread's box_group_id. Use id with hey set-aside group create/add/remove and hey move; use topic_id with hey thread read.

flags.name: limit
flags.desc: Maximum number of threads to show

commands.name: setup
commands.short: Set up HEY for first use
commands.notes: Runs the first-run wizard: OAuth sign-in, a look at the linked accounts, coding-agent setup, and the Omarchy integration when detected. --skip-agents and --skip-omarchy leave those integrations unchanged. --silent-success keeps required authentication and failure output, shows an installation spinner, and ends with SETUP COMPLETE. HEY_NONINTERACTIVE=1 suppresses interactive sign-in, but unskipped agent setup still writes skill files and the wizard persists the onboarded flag — there is no read-only mode; use `hey doctor` to inspect without changing anything. --json changes only the output format: a terminal on stdin (an allocated PTY included) still starts browser OAuth and waits for it. Logged out and non-interactive reports status incomplete with a remediation breadcrumb.

flags.name: silent-success
flags.desc: Show setup activity and end a successful run with SETUP COMPLETE

subcommands.name: agents
subcommands.short: Install or remove HEY coding-agent integrations
subcommands.notes: Never prompts. Set HEY_SETUP_AGENT=claude|codex|all|none to choose; unset auto-detects a single agent. --remove uninstalls HEY's managed agent integrations.

subcommands.name: claude
subcommands.notes: Non-interactive when output is piped or --json is set. Succeeds with {plugin_installed, agent_detected}; a not-detected or not-connected outcome is an error envelope (code setup_incomplete, manual steps in the hint) with a nonzero exit.

subcommands.name: codex
subcommands.notes: Non-interactive when output is piped or --json is set. Succeeds with {plugin_installed, agent_detected}; a not-detected or not-connected outcome is an error envelope (code setup_incomplete, manual steps in the hint) with a nonzero exit.

subcommands.name: omarchy
subcommands.short: Install hey into the Omarchy desktop
subcommands.notes: Only meaningful on Omarchy Linux. Writes to ~/.config/omarchy and ~/.local/share/applications; never edits Hyprland keybindings.

flags.name: notify
flags.desc: Turn on the bar plugin's new-mail toasts

flags.name: remove
flags.desc: Remove everything hey setup omarchy installed

commands.name: share
commands.short: Get a sharing link for an email thread
commands.notes: Accepts the topic_id from hey box view, hey label view, or hey search output. Returns the sharing link in the url field.

commands.name: shell-completion
commands.short: Set up tab completion for your shell
commands.notes: Subcommands: install, generate. install writes the script where the shell reads it and is the usual way in; generate prints it to stdout for a package or a dotfile to place itself.

subcommands.name: generate
subcommands.short: Print a completion script to stdout

subcommands.name: install
subcommands.short: Install shell completions where your shell will find them
subcommands.notes: Writes one file under the user's home. Reports the path it wrote and any shell configuration still needed.

flags.name: force
flags.desc: Write even over a packaged or foreign completion file

subcommands.name: install
subcommands.short: Install the hey skill globally for your coding agents

commands.name: snippet
commands.short: List and manage reusable email snippets
commands.notes: List, create, update, or delete snippets. Find snippet IDs with hey snippet list.

subcommands.name: create

flags.name: content-html
flags.desc: Snippet content as raw HTML instead of Markdown

examples: hey snippet create --name "Scheduling reply" --content "Tuesday works for me."

hey snippet create --name "Office hours" --content "

Office hours are Monday through Thursday.

"

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.notes: Returns snippet IDs, names, plain text, and rich-text HTML. Use an ID with hey snippet update or delete.

subcommands.name: update

flags.name: content-html
flags.desc: New snippet content as raw HTML instead of Markdown

examples: hey snippet update 44 --content "Wednesday works for me."

commands.name: spam
commands.notes: Accepts one or more box item IDs from hey box view output. Marks each thread as spam and removes it from the current box.

commands.name: stop-ignoring
commands.notes: Accepts one or more box item IDs from hey box view output. Reverses hey ignore for each thread.

commands.name: thread
commands.notes: Subcommands: read. Thread IDs come from hey box view. Use the same ID with hey reply or hey forward.

subcommands.name: read
subcommands.notes: Returns a thread with all entries, oldest first. Entry bodies are Markdown; the creator is the account user, while a non-default send-as address is the optional sender on a hydrated entry. Each entry whose message was read carries recipients as to, cc and bcc contact lists. In JSON, inbound entries also carry received_via: the exact account delivery addresses HEY recorded, distinct from the visible recipients, with an optional resolved contact. --html writes an HTML document instead, one <article> per entry with a From/To/CC/BCC header and HEY's original body HTML. A thread that could only be read in part is refused unless --allow-partial is passed, in which case each entry's body_state says what was read. Use the topic ID with hey reply or hey forward.

flags.name: allow-partial
flags.desc: Take a thread that could only be read in part, with a notice saying what is missing

commands.name: timetrack
commands.notes: Subcommands: start, stop, current, list, edit, delete, export, categories, category. Use current to check if tracking is active before start/stop. Stop takes --category to file the track as it stops it. List, edit and delete work on completed tracks and take the IDs list reports. Export writes CSV to stdout or safely saves it with --output.

flags.name: category
flags.desc: Category title to file the track under, created if HEY has none by that title

flags.name: end
flags.desc: New end, as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM in your time zone

flags.name: start
flags.desc: New start, as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM in your time zone

subcommands.name: export
subcommands.short: Export completed time tracks as CSV
subcommands.notes: Writes HEY's CSV unchanged to stdout. Use --output to save it to a file; existing paths are preserved unless --force is set. The columns are Start, End, Duration, Category, and Notes.

flags.name: output
flags.desc: Save CSV to this file instead of stdout

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.notes: Reads HEY's tracked time index, newest-ended first. Category is a title and is empty for an unfiled track. --category takes a category ID from hey timetrack categories.

flags.name: category
flags.desc: Only tracks filed under this category ID

flags.name: limit
flags.desc: Maximum number of time tracks to show

flags.name: category
flags.desc: Category title to file the stopped track under, created if HEY has none by that title

commands.name: todo
commands.notes: Subcommands: list, add, complete, uncomplete, delete. Use list --ids-only to pipe IDs to complete/delete.

flags.name: calendar
flags.desc: Calendar ID to read (defaults to the personal calendar)

flags.name: limit
flags.desc: Maximum number of todos to show

commands.name: trash
commands.notes: Accepts one or more box item IDs from hey box view output. Shared threads lose your access rather than being deleted for everyone.

flags.name: instance
flags.desc: Name this TUI for remote open requests

flags.name: remote
flags.desc: Open the destination in a running TUI and exit

flags.name: topic
flags.desc: Open a thread by topic ID

flags.name: topic-title
flags.desc: Set the title of a directly opened thread

commands.name: unseen
commands.notes: Accepts one or more box item IDs from hey box view output. Marks each email thread as unseen/unread.

commands.name: unshare
commands.short: Turn off an email thread's sharing link
commands.notes: Accepts the topic_id from hey box view, hey label view, or hey search output. The thread remains in HEY.

commands.name: upgrade
commands.short: Upgrade hey to the latest release
commands.notes: Exits 0 only when already current or when the upgrade was applied and confirmed. An optional version argument pins the target release for native and mise installs; upgrades never downgrade. Error codes: upgrade_required (an update exists but this install method must be upgraded another way — follow the hint), upgrade_incomplete, upgrade_unverified, upgrade_failed.

commands.name: watch
commands.short: Follow email threads and calendars as they change
commands.notes: Long-running. Writes one JSON object per changed thread to stdout (NDJSON), not the usual envelope. Use --exit-on-first to block until one change lands and then exit.

flags.name: box
flags.desc: Box whose changes to report, by name or ID (repeatable, defaults to all; every box is followed either way, so new mail is judged across all of them)

flags.name: events
flags.desc: Changes to report: added, updated, deleted, resync and new for mail; recording_added, recording_updated, recording_deleted, calendar_added, calendar_updated, calendar_deleted and calendar_resync for the calendars

flags.name: run-async
flags.desc: Shell command to spawn per change, without waiting for it

flags.name: run-sync
flags.desc: Shell command to run per change, one at a time, waiting for each

flags.name: since
flags.desc: Report changes since this time first (RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD)

flags.name: timeout
flags.desc: Give up waiting after this long (for example 30m)

commands.name: workflow
commands.notes: The workflow ID comes from hey workflow list. Detail returns stage IDs in position order.

subcommands.name: add
subcommands.short: Add email threads to a workflow stage

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.notes: Returns workflow IDs, names, and linked account IDs. Use an ID with hey workflow view; use --account to limit the list to one linked mail account.

flags.name: limit
flags.desc: Maximum number of workflows to show

subcommands.name: move
subcommands.short: Move email threads to another workflow stage

subcommands.name: remove
subcommands.short: Remove email threads from a workflow

subcommands.name: stage
subcommands.notes: Create adds an Untitled stage; use hey workflow view <id> to find its stage ID, then update it with --name.

subcommands.name: create
subcommands.short: Add an Untitled stage to a workflow

subcommands.name: view
subcommands.short: View a workflow and its stages
subcommands.notes: The workflow ID comes from hey workflow list. Detail returns stage IDs in position order.
